contentHtml:
The API is running and its readiness check can read PostgreSQL, but customers cannot create reservations. In this disposable deployment, the candidate image stays the same while a database access configuration changes. Restore the specific permission that failed and verify the result through the HTTP route a customer uses.

Build, test and deploy

The CI workflow builds the reservation service once from a recorded Git revision. It runs the API/worker contention test against that image, then starts the recovery drill in a separate Compose project with its own database volume. The API and worker container image IDs must match the tested image ID. A tag alone would also identify another build if someone moved the tag.

The workflow runs on pull requests that affect the service or the executable drill. To repeat it on the default branch, select the reservation recovery workflow in GitHub Actions and use Run workflow. Open the run summary for the test result, commit and image ID. Its downloadable evidence includes the contention test output, the pipeline record and the deployment timeline.

Recorded drill

On 2026-11-24, CI passed the API/worker contention test for revision ff7ffed. The drill verified that both deployed containers used the tested image ID, sha256:3170ece157c3e04417fd76dcb01382cef7638f0906465ac180da5468514348b9, and checked both IDs again after recovery. CI run · Tested revision · Pipeline record · Contention test output

Time (UTC) Observation
00:49:41.041 The API confirmed control reservation control-42 for Ana on slot 42. PostgreSQL held the matching row.
00:49:41.117 The first scheduled probe booked slot 1001. The drill then revoked the application's insert privilege.
00:49:43.118 The booking for slot 1002 returned 500 InternalError. The API logged InsufficientPrivilege for the same claim, probe-1002.
00:49:45.118 Slot 1003 also returned 500. During the fault, /ready returned 200 and the control reservation was still present.
00:49:45.338 PostgreSQL confirmed that the restored grant allowed inserts again.
00:49:47.120 Slot 1004 returned 201 Confirmed. PostgreSQL held probe-1004, the earlier success on slot 1001 and the original control. Neither failed claim had a row.

Observed booking recovery took 4.002 seconds (00:49:47.120 minus 00:49:43.118). Probes ran every two seconds with zero missed samples. The interval includes the wait for a second failure before the automatic repair and the wait for the next booking probe. To reproduce the calculation, use the completed_utc values for slots 1002 and 1004 in the deployment and probe record.

Follow the drill

Phase Operator action and evidence
Baseline Make a synthetic booking through the API on loopback. Check its owner and claim ID from PostgreSQL. Keep this reservation as the control.
Deploy the fault Revoke the application role's INSERT on slot_claims in the lab database. Each subsequent booking probe uses a different existing, unclaimed slot and its own claim ID.
Diagnose Capture the first failed POST, its UTC response time and claim ID. Correlate the API log's InsufficientPrivilege with that claim and verify the effective privilege. GET /ready can still return 200 because its query only reads the parent slot.
Recover Restore INSERT to the same role on that table. The next successful probe must return 201 Confirmed for a fresh claim. Verify the corresponding row and the original control in PostgreSQL.

The role also serves the worker, so the faulty grant can affect both write paths. This drill measures recovery of the public-facing API operation. A 409 SlotTaken would indicate an occupied fixture and invalidate the measurement. If the error, image ID or stored row differs from the expected evidence, investigate the discrepancy before declaring recovery.

The two configuration changes below are performed by the drill's database operator only inside its private Compose project.

REVOKE INSERT ON slot_claims FROM reservation_app;
GRANT INSERT ON slot_claims TO reservation_app;

The drill runner probes on a two-second schedule. Subtract the UTC timestamp of the first failed booking response from the UTC timestamp of the first confirmed response after the grant is restored. This is the customer-visible interval observed by the probes. A repair between probes is observable only on a later sample. Keep the sampling interval with the result when comparing drills.

Repeat locally and reset

Use Linux, Git, Python 3 and Docker with Compose supporting up --wait. Start at the repository root on a clean checkout of the revision you intend to test. The first build needs registry and Python package index access. The following commands build a candidate from that checkout and run the lab with the image you just built. The GitHub workflow also runs the #21 contention test before deploying the candidate.

export SOURCE_REVISION=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
export RESERVATION_IMAGE="reservation-ci:$SOURCE_REVISION"
docker build --label "org.opencontainers.image.revision=$SOURCE_REVISION" \
  -t "$RESERVATION_IMAGE" examples/reference-implementations/small-production-service/reservations
export EXPECTED_IMAGE_ID=$(docker image inspect --format '{{.Id}}' "$RESERVATION_IMAGE")
records=$(mktemp -d)
python3 examples/operational-scenarios/deployment-and-rollback/reservation-recovery/drill.py \
  --output "$records/drill.json"

The runner creates a fresh project, selects an available loopback port and removes its containers, network and volume at the end. To reset and repeat, run it again with a new output file. Keep the previous JSON to compare runs. If your Docker daemon has exhausted its address pool, set RESERVATION_SUBNET to an unused private CIDR before starting.

For recovery decisions, see the deployment rollback runbook. PostgreSQL documents how grants from multiple sources determine effective access and how to query it. REVOKE and privilege inquiry functions.
